title: What's social about social learning?
type: Journal article (theoretical review / position paper in a special issue of Journal of Comparative Psychology).
central_question: Whether social learning depends on distinct, social-specific learning mechanisms (cognitive adaptations for group living) or on the same domain-general associative mechanisms as asocial learning; and, if the latter, what then makes social learning "social".
framework: - Three types of social learning mapped onto three types of asocial learning (from Heyes, 1994): stimulus enhancement = single-stimulus (S) learning; observational conditioning = S-S (Pavlovian) learning; observational learning/imitation = S/R learning, which subdivides into R-S ("goal-directed imitation") and S-R ("blind imitation").
limitations: - The associative claim does not imply that all learning is associative, nor that all social cognition is social learning.
extra_ingredients: socially biased input mechanisms: perception, attention, motivation
